Prolonged integration friction following the BB&T/SunTrust merger and the subsequent divestiture of Truist Insurance Holdings (TIH) leave a commoditized spread-lending institution lacking structural pricing power against national money-center banks and private credit.

In 2024, Truist divested its highest-return, capital-light subsidiary (Truist Insurance Holdings) to Stone Point and CD&R to bolster regulatory capital and fund share buybacks. As a fractional-reserve commercial deposit bank, it faces high deposit betas, commoditized asset yields, and inherent credit and duration risks (g6_default: N).

qualitative.evidence: Wells Fargo is a 'Big Four' US diversified bank with ~$1.4T in deposits and ~4,000 branches. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 13.64% with ROTCE expanding to 16.3% by 2026. The French retail network experienced severe margin compression when ECB rates rose due to fixed-rate loan portfolios and mandated pass-through deposit costs.

Proven high ROE (13-18%) across cycles. Primary erosion risks include digital fintech disintermediation and macroeconomic commodity/oil shocks affecting Norwegian credit.

Dominant Norwegian retail and commercial bank with strong ~30% market share and low-cost deposit moat, but disqualified at Gate 6 due to inherent commercial fractional-reserve banking leverage (>10x assets/equity) and deposit duration/credit risk.
qualitative.evidence: DNB holds ~30% market share in Norwegian retail mortgages and corporate lending with strong ROE (15-18% in FY23-FY25, net income NOK 41.9B in FY25). However, as a commercial deposit bank, it operates with fractional-reserve leverage (assets/equity >10x) and wholesale debt funding, failing the Gate 6 non-bank fortress balance sheet requirement.

qualitative.3m: Leading retail and SME banking franchise in Austria and Central & Eastern Europe with sticky customer deposit bases and high local market shares. Demonstrated high ROTE (16-17%). Primary erosion risks include sovereign regulatory interventions (bank asset levies and windfall taxes across CEE) and fintech payment disintermediation.

Regional retail banking franchise across Central and Eastern Europe faces persistent terminal headwinds from arbitrary sovereign bank taxes (Hungary, Romania, Slovakia), geopolitical exposure on the EU eastern flank, and digital fintech disintermediation.
qualitative.evidence: Erste Group generates strong profitability (ROTE 16-17% in 2023-2025) across Austria and CEE, but its runway is capped by frequent government interventions (windfall taxes, interest rate caps, currency volatility) in its eastern markets and digital banking disruption, reducing CAP below the 15-year hurdle.

qualitative.3m: Digital-first pan-European banking scale enables a superior cost-to-income ratio compared to traditional branch networks, but core products remain commoditized and rate-cyclical.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y reduced by -10Y for European digital banking rivalry (4_riv=1), zero-cost deposit switching (4_buy=1), and neo-bank platform substitution (4_sub=1).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Branchless digital banking cost advantage is eroding as incumbent peers close branches and neo-banks (Revolut, N26, Bunq) commoditize digital deposits. Group earnings are over 75% dependent on rate-sensitive Net Interest Income (NII), failing the 15-year secular resilience test.
qualitative.evidence: ING Groep serves ~38M retail and wholesale customers across the Benelux and Germany. However, revenue is structurally dominated by net interest margins which collapsed during the ECB's negative interest rate era (2014-2022). With zero-cost digital deposit switching and aggressive neo-bank competition, competitive advantage persistence cannot be underwritten for 15+ years.

qualitative.evidence: Investec operates across the UK and South Africa (~50% operating profit from Southern Africa). Group ROTE historically averaged 10-14%, heavily dependent on South African macro conditions and Rand exchange rates. Wealth management fees face ongoing industry-wide fee compression, and specialist lending offers zero independent pricing power above benchmark rates.

qualitative.evidence: Intesa Sanpaolo generates superior returns on tangible equity (ROTE 15-18%) powered by captive wealth management (Eurizon, Fideuram). However, with total assets exceeding €900B against ~€55B in tangible equity, it relies fundamentally on fractional-reserve leverage, deposit duration transformation, and ECB liquidity backstops. Commercial deposit banks fail Gate 6 by design under the Munger peace-of-mind balance sheet standard.

qualitative.evidence: FY2024-2025 ROE reached 14-15% with Net Profit of €3.4B-€3.6B and CET1 ratio of 14.9% (Basel IV). Solvency II ratio for insurance operations stands at 227%. However, total balance sheet leverage exceeds 12x assets-to-equity (€27.3B long-term debt, €34.0B cash, €350B+ total assets), exposing equity to systemic credit cycles, deposit run dynamics, and regulatory liquidity mandates.
